::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at Part 2](../../slides/eu-frames-full.html#/part-2-the-claim-and-its-estimand){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

The original author (OA) asked whether the economic crisis changed how citizens of the European Union frame the Union, and answered from sixteen waves of the Eurobarometer, ten years of surveys in twenty-seven member states. The claim is about countries in years, while the surveys hold respondents, so the analysis rests on a panel of country-years, built by averaging the answers of each country in each year, and on models for such a panel. This stage downloads the sixteen files and turns them into the panel with the scripts of the workspace, writes the estimand statement and the causal graph, and reproduces a recorded result with the models behind it. It takes about six and three quarter hours with the download and the build, and about five without them.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" icon=false}
**The licence of the files.** The Eurobarometer files come under the terms of use of GESIS, which forbid passing them on, publishing anything about individual respondents, and processing them with an AI assistant. They stay on your own machine, out of every repository and out of any session that an AI assistant can read. The panel that the workspace ships is an aggregate, to which none of these restrictions applies.
:::

## 1. The Eurobarometer files

[45 minutes]{.text-muted}

[Download the Eurobarometer files](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-eurobarometer-files-for-the-individual-level-work){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Register with GESIS, which is free and immediate, and download the Stata file of each of the sixteen studies, about half a gigabyte in all. The setup page of the AR4DS site gives the steps, and [the GESIS archive](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-gesis) in the module on data sources takes the same steps screen by screen. Read what the terms of use allow and what they forbid.

## 2. Building the analysis file

[60 minutes]{.text-muted}

[Open Building the analysis file](../../companion/data-management.qmd#sec-eu-frames){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Run the first script of the workspace on your sixteen files and read the report that it prints. Then work through the second, which scores the items into scales, deals with the respondents who named nothing, averages the respondents into country-years with and without survey weights, merges the macro series, and reproduces the panel of the course.

## 3. The country-year level

[20 minutes]{.text-muted}

[Open The country-year level](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-aggregation){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The first section of the module on statistical methods says why the predictor is measured at the country-year, and what a cell mean is a mean of.

## 4. The claim and its estimand

[45 minutes]{.text-muted}

**On the slides**, from the start of Part 2. The slides present the paper of the OA, the claim as the analysts received it, the model that the OA fitted and the five questions that the analysts asked of the claim. The slides go on to the run on estimands with the red-card study as the example, and to the short course on causal graphs, and end on the estimand statement and the graph of the claim, half built. The run of slides on R, from "R, in one slide" to "Common error messages", repeats stage 2 and can be skipped.

## 5. Task 2 – The panel, the estimand and the graph

[30 minutes]{.text-muted}

**In your report** or your working script, or in the browser lab.

[Open the browser lab at Task 2](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-2-get-the-data-and-look-at-it){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

Draw the outcome of the panel country by country, and find the countries that move sharply around 2009. Write the [estimand statement](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-4-estimand-and-dag) with every bracket filled. Open `R/dag_starter.R`, keep the arrows that you are willing to defend, and write two sentences on what two-way fixed effects adjust for and what they cannot fix.

## 6. Causal graphs on a panel

[45 minutes]{.text-muted}

[Open Causal graphs and adjustment sets at section 3](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-eu-frames){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Read [the section on the EU-frames case](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-eu-frames) of the module on causal graphs. It covers graphs written as formulas, a collider in a regression, the graph of the case and its adjustment set, the limits of fixed effects, and the bailout on the graph. If the short course on the slides left confounders, mediators and colliders unclear, read [Arrows as claims](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-arrows) and [Confounder, mediator, collider](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-shapes) first.

## 7. Task 3 – The reproduction

[40 minutes]{.text-muted}

**On the slides, then in your report** or in the browser lab.

[Open the deck at Part 3](../../slides/eu-frames-full.html#/part-3-reproduction-and-exploration){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Open the browser lab at Task 3](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The opening slides of Part 3 read the instruction of Task 2 of Multi100. Then reproduce one of the three analyses that the lab and the workspace offer, and refit it until the value on record comes back to the third decimal: t = −3.804 for C6HJR, t = −7.169 for KQXUE and t = −1.206 for 018OL. The [exercise overview](../../cases/eu-frames/exercise.qmd) lists the three analyses with their data and their models, and in the lab each gap to fill has a hint and a solution, which are worth opening only after a try of your own.

## 8. The models of a panel

[120 minutes]{.text-muted}

[Open The statistical methods behind the course at section 2](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-ols){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Work from [The linear model](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-ols) to [Standard errors with few clusters](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-inference). The sections take a regression in its plainest form, the straight line with noise of which every later model is a variation, and then clustered standard errors and what they correct. The sections go on to the two designs of fixed effects, for country and year together and for country alone, and end on standard errors with few clusters, with the CR2 correction and its Satterthwaite degrees of freedom.

**Shortcuts.** Without a GESIS account, or without the time and the disk space that the download takes, skip the download and read the data-management module without running it, since the module quotes what the scripts print and the panel of the workspace is the one that the scripts rebuild. If you have drawn causal graphs for panel data before, read only [the limits of fixed effects](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-growth) in the graph module. If you have fitted regressions with controls before, skip the linear model.

**By the end of the stage** you have the panel of the course rebuilt from your own sixteen files, or the module that rebuilds it read; the estimand behind the claim written in one sentence, with a graph that holds only the arrows that you are willing to defend; a recorded result reproduced to the third decimal; and two sentences on what two-way fixed effects absorb and what they leave.
